_meta.slice: S2 — broadband / dam / STR + stadium + breadth. ADDITIVE to S1 (same Franklin; references S1 entities by seed_key). Pipeline loads s1 then s2.
_meta.shape: LOGICAL, same conventions as S1. Council measures (CM-*) are voted by Watauga councilmembers (off-finch…off-tanner + mayor off-bell); state bills (HB-*) by the 10 delegates. Open/closing-soon proposals have NO final vote (in deliberation); closed proposals carry a roll call.
_meta.storylines: CM-22 broadband = cross-level (B-2); HB-09 dam = slow deliberation + FDEQ Q&A (B-3, see qa.json); CM-15 STR = heated-but-civil local (B-4). CM-19 stadium = the light one. HB-21/HB-18/HB-07/CM-11/CM-24 = breadth (records + light positions, window-state variety).

proposals.title: Watauga Broadband Measure
proposals.summary_plain: A municipal broadband bond, paired with a state-subsidy match, to build fiber across Watauga and out to the county lines. The cross-level question: does the city match reach the rural plateau, or just re-wire neighborhoods that already have service?
sections: Title I — Municipal bond for a city fiber backbone.
Title II — State-subsidy match (links to a Franklin appropriation; the cross-level graph edge).
Title III — Build-out requirement: open question whether to tie the match to county-line coverage.

proposals.title: Valley Water Rights Act
proposals.summary_plain: Allocates Nolichucky and French Broad withdrawal rights among farms, Watauga municipal supply, and in-stream conservation flow. The slow, technical deliberation — and the policy backdrop to the Pigeon River dam relicensing FDEQ is running.
sections: Title I — Agricultural withdrawal allocations + metering.
Title II — Municipal supply guarantees for Watauga.
Title III — Minimum in-stream flow for conservation + fisheries.

proposals.title: Short-Term Rental Ordinance
proposals.summary_plain: Caps short-term rentals in downtown Watauga. A heated-but-civil local fight: housing cost and neighborhood character vs. small-business and homeowner income. Ward interests split (Coley/Massey resist).
sections: Title I — Downtown STR cap + permit cap.
Title II — Primary-residence carve-out (the B-4 compromise hinge).

proposals.title: Riverside Stadium & Parks Bond
proposals.summary_plain: A bond for a riverside stadium and parks package. The light one — high-volume, low-stakes, some humor. Realistic home for routine noise (and showcase fixtures).

proposals.title: Lobbying Disclosure Act
proposals.summary_plain: Requires PACs to disclose donors above a threshold. The in-world version of what Civitics itself does; quietly opposed by the PACs. The Watauga Open Books initiative drives it (see initiatives.json).
proposals.outcome: Pending; quietly opposed by Cumberland Energy Action Fund and Greater Watauga Forward.

proposals.title: Clean Air Monitoring Act
proposals.summary_plain: Places air-quality sensors across the plateau, including Boyd's Iron Ridge. Cross-pressure: helps Boyd's constituents even though he's a NO on energy.

proposals.title: Coal Heritage Workforce Act
proposals.summary_plain: Retraining + heritage tourism for plateau coal counties. A low-controversy consensus bill — the contrast to HB-14's split.

proposals.title: Participatory Budget Pilot
proposals.summary_plain: Open-data + a small participatory-budgeting pilot. Meta-civic; a finished, archived success.

proposals.title: Mill District Rezoning (Ward 4)
proposals.summary_plain: Rezones the Ward 4 mill district. Jurisdiction-admin archived decision + an evidence-cited land-use fight; demonstrates the closed-window archive view.
